newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Japan prices seen mixed, supply shift likely.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Japan prices seen mixed, supply shift likely.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to be mixed this week with participants continuing to look to the currency market for direction amid a dearth of factors overall, traders said on Monday.
Some traders also said Japanese physical buyers were expected to shift away from high-priced Thai rubber to cheaper Indonesia rubber (Standard Indonesian rubber 20).
"It is possible Japanese buyers could shift to cheaper Indonesian rubber." a trader said.

Thai rubber prices have been relatively firm recently, backed by the Thai government's intervention scheme under which it has started buying rubber from the domestic market at 29.00 baht per kg, up from the previous support price of 27.50 baht.
"Supplies of Indonesian rubber appear to be ample so even if supplies are bought it is unlikely physical or (Japanese) rubber futures prices will be helped," the trader said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at a firm price of 117 U.S. cents per kg on a FOB basis on Monday, although lower than 120 U.S. cents on May 19.
Japanese rubber futures prices are expected to see a slight recovery this week after last week's sharp decline, analysts said.

"After last week's sharp decline in prices which were in response to the yen's steep gains against the dollar, a small technical rebound is likely early in the week," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
"But the upside may be limited as private investors are expected to quickly sell when prices rise, based on a view that the dollar remains vulnerable on the downside," he said.
Weak prices in rubber producing countries, such as Indonesia, may also put a lid on futures' gains here, traders said.
"The TOCOM benchmark's upside at 138 yen is likely to be tough to break through," one technical analyst at a commodity brokerage house said.
The spot May contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) expired at noon at 128.5 yen, up from 128.0 yen, with 499 lots of deliveries.
The market was encouraged by a smaller-than-expected number of deliveries.
TOCOM Benchmark October rubber ended the morning session at 136.3 yen per kg, compared with 133.5 yen last Friday.
On the Kobe Rubber Exchange, benchmark October was quoted at 136.1 yen, compared with 134.3 yen last Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted lower at 148 yen as of Monday, compared with 157 yen on May 19.
The sharp drop in the physical market followed last week's fall in rubber futures markets.
